class.name: ShaderMaterial
class.brief_description: A material defined by a custom [Shader] program and the values of its shader parameters.
class.description: A material that uses a custom [Shader] program to render visual items (canvas items, meshes, skies, fog), or to process particles. Compared to other materials, [ShaderMaterial] gives deeper control over the generated shader code. For more information, see the shaders documentation index below. Multiple [ShaderMaterial]s can use the same shader and configure different values for the shader uniforms. [b]Note:[/b] For performance reasons, the [signal Resource.changed] signal is only emitted when the [member Resource.resource_name] changes. Only in editor, it is also emitted for [member shader] changes.

method.name: get_shader_parameter
method.description: Returns the current value set for this material of a uniform in the shader.

method.name: set_shader_parameter
method.description: Changes the value set for this material of a uniform in the shader. [b]Note:[/b] [param param] is case-sensitive and must match the name of the uniform in the code exactly (not the capitalized name in the inspector). [b]Note:[/b] Changes to the shader uniform will be effective on all instances using this [ShaderMaterial]. To prevent this, use per-instance uniforms with [method GeometryInstance3D.set_instance_shader_parameter] or duplicate the [ShaderMaterial] resource using [method Resource.duplicate]. Per-instance uniforms allow for better shader reuse and are therefore faster, so they should be preferred over duplicating the [ShaderMaterial] when possible.

method.name: set_shader_feature
method.description: [admonition type="note" collapsible="true" open="false"] [b]Part of [i]Godot Engine: Conservatory Edition[/i].[/b] This is not available in the official build of Godot. [/admonition] Enables or disables the provided shader feature. Shader features are added to a shader using [code]#pragma features A B C ...[/code] and operate as static flags. These can be checked using [code]#ifdef A[/code] or [code]#if defined(A)[/code] in the shader. Only features that have been declared in the list can be used in this method. [b]Note:[/b] [param feature] is case-sensitive and must match the name of the feature in the code exactly. Unlike uniforms, the inspector displays these properties verbatim. [b]Note:[/b] For organizational purposes, it is valid to place multiple [code]#pragma features[/code] lines in a shader. All of the lines are collected into one set of features.

method.name: set_shader_variant
method.description: [admonition type="note" collapsible="true" open="false"] [b]Part of [i]Godot Engine: Conservatory Edition[/i].[/b] This is not available in the official build of Godot. [/admonition] Changes to the provided shader variant. Shader variants are added to a shader using [code]#pragma exclusive_variants NAME : A B C ...[/code] and operate as a static "switch". These can be checked using [code]#ifdef NAME_A[/code] or [code]#if defined(NAME_A)[/code] in the shader, [b]note that the name of the variant is prefixed to the value![/b]. Only variants that have been declared in the list can be selected. [b]Note:[/b] [param variant] is case-sensitive and must match the name of the feature in the code exactly. Unlike uniforms, the inspector displays these properties verbatim, and unlike features, only one variant value can be enabled at once for any given name. In the provided example above, [code]NAME[/code] can only be [code]A[/code], [code]B[/code], or [code]C[/code] [i]exclusively[/i]. Combinations of values are [b]not possible[/b]. [b]Note:[/b] While checked in shaders using the name and value [code]NAME_A[/code], the [param value] parameter must [b]only be the name[/b] ([code]A[/code], [i]not[/i] [code]NAME_A[/code])!

members.member: The [Shader] program used to render this material.
